rationale: The answer covers all three key points accurately. (1) Creation: the AP delivers a basket (or cash) and receives newly issued shares, so shares outstanding increase. (2) Redemption: the AP returns creation units, the fund cancels them, and shares outstanding decrease. (3) Secondary-market trading leaves shares outstanding unchanged because ownership simply transfers between investors. The extra details are accurate and incidental: typical creation unit sizes, transactions at NAV, AP-only primary-market activity, and the arbitrage role. There are no material errors.
